say: A partial budget lists only what changes when you switch. For example, Rukayat's hybrid gave 923 kg per hectare more than her usual seed. At about 600 naira per kg, that is 553,800 naira of added income.

card.title: Rukayat's added costs for Variety A

say: Now the added costs. Hybrid seed costs 100,000 naira, minus her usual saved seed worth 14,000, so 86,000 naira extra.

card.title: Rukayat's added costs for Variety A

say: The hybrid needs about one extra bag of fertiliser, roughly 40,000 naira.

card.title: Rukayat's added costs for Variety A

say: Harvesting, shelling, bags and transport for the extra grain add about 15,000 naira.

card.title: Rukayat's added costs for Variety A

say: Her total added costs are 141,000 naira.

card.title: Rukayat's added costs for Variety A

say: Net benefit is the added income minus the added costs. For Rukayat, 553,800 minus 141,000 is 412,800 naira.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs

say: The marginal rate of return is net benefit divided by the extra money spent. Here it is about 293%. Farming is risky, so aim for 50% to 100% or more.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs

say: Break-even is added costs divided by the grain price. 141,000 divided by 600 is 235 kg. Below that gain, she loses money.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs

say: If the price drops to 400 naira at harvest, her net benefit is still 228,200 naira.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs

say: But if a dry spell cuts the gain to 200 kg, she loses money that year.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs

say: Use the price you will actually receive, not the highest price you have heard.

panel.heading: Net benefit, return and break-even
items: Net benefit: income minus added costs
panel.rule: Always test against a lower price and a bad season.

say: Seed is alive, and heat and moisture make it age fast. Dry it on a clean tarpaulin or raised mat.

panel.heading: Dry it, test it, seal it
items: Dry on a tarpaulin, not bare soil
Avoid hot zinc or concrete at midday
Salt jar test: seed plus dry salt
Seal in airtight bags, off the floor

say: Avoid very hot zinc roofing or concrete at midday, which can damage the seed.

say: Then do the salt jar test. Put a handful of seed and two or three spoons of dry salt in a dry glass jar. Shake it and wait about 15 minutes.

say: If salt sticks to the jar, the seed is still too damp. Dry it longer and test again.

say: Store it in airtight bags such as PICS bags, which starve weevils of oxygen. Label each one.

say: If you use a storage insecticide, use only an approved product at the label dose, and keep planting seed apart from food grain.

panel.rule: Keep seed dry, keep it cool, keep air and insects out.

say: In a community seed bank, members borrow seed at planting and return more after harvest. For example, a women's group in Benue State starts with 60 kg of certified cowpea seed.

panel.heading: A women's cowpea seed bank
items: New stock: 92 kg, all seed tested

say: Twelve members borrow 4 kg each.

panel.heading: A women's cowpea seed bank
items: New stock: 92 kg, all seed tested

say: After harvest, ten members return double, 8 kg each. That is 80 kg.

panel.heading: A women's cowpea seed bank
items: New stock: 92 kg, all seed tested

say: Two members lost their crops to flooding. The group records 8 kg as owed next season.

panel.heading: A women's cowpea seed bank
items: New stock: 92 kg, all seed tested

say: The stock grows to 92 kg. Every returned lot gets a germination test, and one poor lot is kept for food, not seed.

say: Write your decision rules before you see the results. For example, Hauwa in Kano adopts only if a variety wins in all three blocks and the return is above 100%.
Variety A meets every rule. But she plants it on half her land, not all, because one season is limited evidence.
Variety B won on average but not in every block, and its return was only 45%. She re-tests it on a small area, and keeps her usual seed as insurance.
Write a short, honest report. Give your goal and the varieties, your methods and layout, and season notes like dry spells or animal damage.
Put the results in a table with corrected yields, then your partial budget and your decision. Say plainly what did not work.

panel.heading: What your trial report contains
items: Goal and varieties, with seed source

say: To remember. A partial budget lists only what changes. Test a lower price and a bad season. Dry seed and check it with the salt test, then store it airtight. And set your rules before you see the results.

panel.heading: Remember
items: List only the costs and income that change

Set decision rules before the results
